hyps.why: Replacing a removed direct edge adds a whole path, whereas replacing another op only swaps one.
Reconnecting the input to node 1 enables all downstream paths through node 1.
Restoring the 2->3 edge adds a path into the output.
Reconnecting input to node 2 adds a path that was missing.
A strong direct path already provides capacity, so the extra conv gives diminishing returns.
The skip's benefit is partly redundant when a strong conv path already reaches the output.
With edge 1 also removed, the input is cut off from nodes 1 and 2.
Removing the direct edge when edge 1 is already absent leaves very few usable paths.
Edge 2 only helps if node 1 carries a useful signal from a conv on edge 0.
Edge 4 exploits good node-1 features produced by a conv on edge 0.
